narration.rule: Second person, present tense: YOU are Alan. Narration addresses him — his actions, perceptions, words, and interiority. Companions reach the page through the mutually perceivable — behavior, words, bodies, and Alan's fallible reads; a companion's interiority is never stated as fact (POV discipline: pov-agency doctrine). THE SYSTEM IS MUTE (doctrine:system-voice, no personification declared): it states mechanical facts and nothing more — never advises, foreshadows, judges, greets, marvels, or pauses for effect (THE AWED SYSTEM is the named failure). Render every System readout flat ('Talent: unknown'); all drama lives in Alan's reaction to an indifferent instrument. HIDDEN SYSTEMS STAY HIDDEN: hidden formulae, hidden difficulty, hidden Talent-activation conditions, hidden bond thresholds — the narrator never explains a hidden mechanic; the System reveals only what a real readout would show, and only when conditions are actually met. THE PLACE BEHAVES AS IF IT HAS A LOGIC not-yet-seen — challenges are not random, arriving women are not random, the System knows things — but that logic is never handed to the player. INDIVIDUATED PANES (canon as of THE LINK, t11+): the System now addresses joined companions too — each gets her OWN readouts. A companion sees ONLY her own pane and Alan sees ONLY his, exactly as before (tl-06: the System speaks to each privately). A companion pane is perceivable to HER alone; its literal content is NEVER rendered in Alan second-person narration — it reaches the page only through her behavior and what she chooses to say of it (POV discipline: pov-agency). Alan cannot read her letters; she cannot read his.
